styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, galleries and the river's history.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Koalas, river cruises and green escapes.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Markets, laneway cafés and riverside dining.

stays.why: Walk to the river, Queen Street Mall and the CityCat ferries. Best base for first-timers.
Nightlife, live music and cheap eats. A short walk or one train stop from the CBD.
Riverside parklands, the lagoon beach and museums. Family-friendly and walkable.
Relaxed cafés and markets, close to South Bank. Good value for longer stays.

food: Try a classic café breakfast: eggs, sourdough and good coffee. Brisbane takes coffee seriously.
Eat at the markets: weekend farmers' markets and the West End markets have cheap, fresh food.
Seafood by the river: fish and chips at South Bank or along the waterfront.
Fortitude Valley and West End have the widest range of Asian and Middle Eastern cheap eats.
Book ahead for riverside dinners on Friday and Saturday nights. Check opening hours on the day.
more_time: Swap a city day for a day trip to the koala sanctuary at Lone Pine. Check transport and entry prices on the day.
Take a CityCat ferry up the river for a cheap scenic ride instead of a paid cruise.
Add a day at Moreton Island or Stradbroke Island if you have a spare day. Book ferries ahead.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the river, South Bank and the museums, with time for a koala sanctuary or a day trip.

month_notes: January: hot and wet. Highs near 29°C, about 16 rain days. Plan indoor sights and carry a rain jacket.
February: hot and wet, similar to January. Around 13 rain days. Mornings are best for walking.
March: still warm and wet, about 16 rain days. Highs near 28°C. Keep plans flexible.
April: cooler and drier. Highs near 26°C, about 8 rain days. Great month for outdoor days.
May: mild and dry. Highs near 23°C, about 7 rain days. Comfortable for walking and ferries.
June: cool and dry. Highs near 21°C, lows near 11°C. Bring a jacket for evenings.
July: the coolest month. Highs near 21°C, lows near 10°C, about 6 rain days. Pack warm layers.
August: cool and dry, highs near 23°C. About 5 rain days. Good for outdoor plans.
September: warming up, highs near 25°C, about 7 rain days. Pleasant and mostly dry.
October: warm, highs near 26°C, about 10 rain days. Showers return; carry a light rain jacket.
November: hot and wetter, highs near 28°C, about 11 rain days. Start early to beat the heat.
December: hot and wet, highs near 29°C, about 12 rain days. Book indoor backup plans.

climate_guide.summary: Subtropical: warm to hot most of the year, with a wet summer and a mild, dry winter.

items.title: Best time: April to September
items.text: Mild highs of 21–26°C and few rain days. Ideal for walking, ferries and day trips.

items.title: Wet summer (December to March)
items.text: About 12–16 rain days a month. Showers can be heavy but often short. Carry a rain jacket.

items.title: Hot and humid in summer
items.text: Highs near 28–29°C with muggy air. Plan outdoor sights for early morning.

items.title: Cool winter nights
items.text: June to August lows drop to 10–11°C. Bring a jacket for evenings by the river.

items.title: Rain is uneven
items.text: August is the driest month with about 5 rain days. January and March are the wettest.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light layers, a rain jacket, sunscreen and a hat. Add a warm layer for winter evenings.

transit.best: Walk the CBD and South Bank, then use the 50c Translink fares and CityCat ferries for longer trips.

modes.text: Brisbane Metro M1 and M2 buses run every 5–15 minutes along the busway. Fast and frequent.
Translink buses cover the city. A 50c flat fare covers most trips with up to 3 transfers.
Translink trains link the CBD with the suburbs and airport line. Same 50c flat fare on most trips.
CityCat ferries are a scenic and practical way to cross the river. A cheap sightseeing ride too.
Uber and DiDi operate; taxis are plentiful and take cards.
Driving is easy outside peak hours, but parking in the CBD is costly.
The CBD is walkable, with riverside paths good for walking and cycling.
